subject: sentences
title: Poems and Sense Words
about: Tiny rhymes: he finds the two words that rhyme, counts the lines that rhyme, and picks the word that tells how something sounds, feels, smells, looks or tastes, or how someone feels. NC RL.1.4 asks first graders to find words and phrases in stories and poems that suggest feelings or appeal to the senses.
tip: Read the rhyme twice with a bouncy voice, and after he answers ask him to make up one more line that rhymes.

cards.q: My dog likes to run. He plays in the sun. Which two words rhyme?
cards.note: Run and sun end with the same sound: un.

cards.q: A little frog went hop, hop, hop. It jumped right to the top. Which two words rhyme?
cards.note: Hop and top end with the same sound: op.

cards.q: Mia likes to bake. She made a big cake. Which two words rhyme?
cards.note: Bake and cake end with the same sound: ake.

cards.q: I see the moon. It will be night soon. Which two words rhyme?
cards.note: Moon and soon end with the same sound: oon.

cards.q: Ben has a bed. His blanket is red. Pick the two rhyming words.
cards.note: Bed and red end with the same sound: ed. Ben starts like bed but ends with n.

cards.q: Up high is a star. It is very far. Pick the two rhyming words.
cards.note: Star and far end with the same sound: ar.

cards.q: Buzz, buzz goes the bee. It flies to the tree. Which word tells how the bee sounds?
cards.note: Buzz is a sound word. Say it and you can hear the bee.

cards.q: Splash! The duck jumps in. It swims with a grin. Which word is a sound word?
cards.note: Splash is a sound word. It is the noise of hitting the water.

cards.q: My cat is soft. I pat her fur. She sits and starts to purr. Which word tells how her fur feels?
cards.note: Soft is a touch word. Purr is a sound word.

cards.q: The snow is cold and white. I catch a flake so light. Which word tells how the snow feels?
cards.note: Cold tells how snow feels. White tells how it looks.

cards.q: The rose smells sweet. It grows by my feet. Which word tells how the rose smells?
cards.note: Sweet is a smell word here. Your nose tells you a rose is sweet.

cards.q: Fresh bread smells so yummy. It warms up my tummy. Which word tells how the bread smells?
cards.note: Yummy tells how the bread smells. Tummy is where the bread goes.

cards.q: The sun is so bright. It gives us light. Which word tells how the sun looks?
cards.note: Bright is a seeing word. Your eyes tell you the sun is bright.

cards.q: The lemon is sour. It is yellow like a flower. Which word tells how the lemon tastes?
cards.note: Sour is a taste word. Yellow tells how the lemon looks.

cards.q: Sam got a new sled. "I am glad," he said. Which word tells how Sam feels?
cards.note: Glad is a feeling word. It means happy.

cards.q: Liv lost her kite. She is sad tonight. Which word tells how Liv feels?
cards.note: Sad is a feeling word. Losing the kite is why she feels that way.

cards.q: I see a bug. It is on the rug. It is very small. How many lines rhyme?
cards.note: Bug and rug rhyme, so two lines rhyme. Small does not rhyme with them.

cards.q: I had a cat. It sat on a mat. It wore a hat. How many lines rhyme?
cards.note: Cat, mat and hat all rhyme, so all three lines rhyme.
